answer: In an attestation graph, trust is estimated by bounded-length random walks, so influence depends on path probability rather than multiplying unchecked. A sybil cluster joined to honest nodes only by a sparse cut has low conductance—the cut weight divided by cluster volume. Given fixed honest seed mass, min-cut and transitivity bounds constrain the trust mass reaching that cluster and thus its aggregate voting weight. Labels such as walnut, meadow, and jade do not change the bound without crossing attestations.
